findings: All five current BPW C2 scored questions are normalized into assessment lineage. The combined route is strongest as shared custody/state/reconciliation workflow; deeper technical specialization should remain split by Backline, Props and Wardrobe later.
Assigned-custody framing matches field-practice evidence around department ownership, but exact custody, signoff and permission rules vary by production and department.
Field-practice evidence supports accurate restoration/packing/organization and state reconciliation as real work outcomes, but no single inventory/checkoff process should be presented as universal.

The combined C2 remains useful for shared work-control concepts, but existing MDQ architecture supports splitting deeper technician/specialist material by Backline, Props and Wardrobe rather than extending one combined technical course indefinitely.
